copy.blurb:
A +18.7pp gap on the France side. Norway v France in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has France stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Public Elo rates France 270 points higher than the other side (Norway 1760, France 2030). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 15%, the draw at 14%, and France to win at 71%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 28%, the draw at 23%, and France to win at 52%. The France side trades at 52% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of −111. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 71%, +18.7pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the France side that lower bound is 64% — +11.3pp clear of the market's 52%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 38 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives France a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +18.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: France are favourites on the market at 52% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 71%, a +18.7pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
copy.title: Norway v France · the model leans France
